## Research Lead: Attention Factors for Statistical Arbitrage (2026-08-27)

**Source**: Epstein, Wang, Choi & Pelger, "Attention Factors for Statistical Arbitrage," accepted ACM ICAIF 2026, arXiv:2510.11616.

**Approach**: 'Attention Factors' -- conditional latent factors learned from firm-characteristic embeddings via an attention mechanism over the cross-section, jointly trained to (1) identify which assets are similar enough to arbitrage against each other, (2) identify mispricing between similar assets, and (3) form a trading policy that maximizes risk-adjusted performance net of transaction costs. This replaces the classical cointegration/correlation approach to picking tradable asset pairs or groups with a learned, characteristic-based similarity metric.

**Reported results**: out-of-sample Sharpe ratio above 4 gross of costs, net Sharpe of **2.3 after transaction costs**, measured on the largest U.S. equities over a 24-year period. Authors include Markus Pelger (Stanford), known for IPCA/conditional-autoencoder factor-model work -- a name that raises confidence this isn't a data-mined result, though it has not been independently replicated here.

**Why this matters for George's pairs-trading gap**: H316 (Moira, arXiv:2605.01954) is currently a STUB blocked on needing an OpenAI-API-driven semantic pair-selection pipeline for LLM-based pair identification. This paper offers a different, non-LLM angle on the identical sub-problem -- "which assets are similar enough to trade against each other" -- via a learned attention/embedding similarity metric instead of GPT-4o semantic classification. It's also directly relevant to the classical pairs-trading family that has twice failed in this wiki: H307 (Johansen cointegration on ETF pairs, IS cointegration anti-predictive of OOS) and H246 (same failure mode, structural breaks). A characteristic-based similarity signal sidesteps the core weakness both of those hypotheses hit -- static cointegration relationships breaking down out of sample -- by construction, since it's retrained/adaptive rather than a single fixed IS-estimated relationship.

**Candidate future hypothesis** (not yet numbered, not yet run): build a simplified version of the asset-similarity signal -- even a plain learned-embedding nearest-neighbor scheme over standard firm characteristics (size, value, momentum, volatility), short of the full attention architecture -- on the existing H241 200-stock universe, and test whether pairs/groups selected by learned similarity outperform pairs selected by Johansen cointegration (H307's approach) or plain sector-membership grouping. Success criterion: OOS Sharpe clears the H241-family gate (1.174) and demonstrably beats a cointegration-selected-pairs control run on the same universe and window. Must audit for the H509-H514 look-ahead bug class -- firm-characteristic embeddings must be computed only from data available as-of the trade date, not refit on the full sample before slicing IS/OOS.

**Related**: [Pairs Trading & Cointegration](pairs-trading.md) (H307/H246 cointegration failures), [LLM Pairs Trading — Moira (STUB, H316)](../sources/) -- complementary non-LLM angle on the same asset-similarity sub-problem.
